scope: Corollary 1.2 (Combined finite-law parameter range) of the manuscript “Self-dual random-cluster interfaces below one” (preprints/Self-dual-random-cluster-interfaces-below-one-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 223 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 bf15a86507a10184), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 9. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For this statement, fix q ∈ (0, 4) and put p(q) = √ q 1 + √ q , κ(q) = 4π arccos(− √ q/2) . Let D be a bounded Jordan domain with smooth simple boundary and distinct boundary marks a, b. Take simple nearest-neighbor lattice polygon approximations Dδn , with δn ↓ 0 and the full closed-polygon graphs specified above, and take aδn , bδn to be distinct polygon vertices. Require counterclockwise parametrizations of ∂Dδn converging uniformly on [0, 1] to one of ∂D, all injective on [0, 1), with the marks aδn , bδn and a, b at parameters 0, 1/2 respectively. Wire all vertices of the counterclockwise arc from bδn to aδn , including its endpoints, leaving the other boundary vertices singleton. Sample (1.2) with this q and p = p(q), and declare wired-arc boundary edges open for drawing. Then the prescribed medial strand, oriented from aδn to bδn , converges in law along the full mesh sequence to chordal SLEκ(q)(D; a, b) in (1.3). No uniformity in q is asserted.
